Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old female with a three-day history of a progressively worsening headache, diffuse with right eye predominance, photophobia, nausea, and neck stiffness; NSAID (ibuprofen) has provided little relief; family history of migraine on maternal side; plan includes trial of stronger analgesia, headache diary, and follow-up to evaluate for migraine and other etiologies.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Headache for ~3 days, described as dull most of the time with episodic sharpness, predominantly around the right eye, global involvement.
- Course and timeline: Onset started at work about 3 days ago, worsened by the next day, and continued to worsen and persist through today; pain present most of the time with fluctuations in intensity (about 8/10 at worst).
- Pain quality and pattern: Gradual onset, dull with intermittent sharp pain; persistent daily symptoms with interspersed peaks.
- Exacerbating factors: Light sensitivity (photophobia) worsens pain; high screen time/work stress noted.
- Alleviating factors: Ibuprofen taken over the last two days with limited relief.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia, nausea/sick feeling; no vomiting reported; neck stiffness noted; no focal neurological symptoms (no weakness, no speech difficulty); no fever or rashes; difficulty focusing at work; some eye discomfort with bright light.
- Vision: No documented loss of vision or significant blurring; light sensitivity and photophobia present.
- Headache history: Has had headaches in the past, but not diagnosed migraines; family history of migraines (mother and sister).
- Medications: Ibuprofen taken; no regular medications reported; no documented allergies.
- Allergies: Not known to be present.
- Social history: Lives with three housemates; IT worker with high screen exposure; socially smokes and drinks; stress related to a new project.
- Eye history: Wears glasses since age 5; no recent eye exam; advised to consider repeat eye testing if symptoms persist or worsen.
- Review of systems: Negative for fever, rashes; positive for photophobia, neck stiffness, nausea; no focal neurologic deficits reported; no speech difficulty; no vision loss.

Past Medical History:
- Headache history described (not migraine diagnosed); family history notable for migraines (mother and sister).
- Regular medications: none.
- Allergies: none known.

Social History:
- Occupation: IT professional with high cognitive load and screen time.
- Living situation: Four-person household (three housemates).
- Substance use: Social smoker; social alcohol use.

Family History:
- Mother and sister have migraines; maternal history notable for migraines.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented in transcript (no vitals or detailed neuro/eye exam provided).

Investigations:
- None reported.

Assessments & Plan:
Issue 1: Migraine-type headache with possible genetic predisposition
- Assessment: Headache characteristics (unilateral/right-eye predominant, photophobia, nausea, gradual progression over 3 days) with significant impact on function and positive family history suggest migraine without aura; NSAID response has been inadequate this time.
- Plan:
  - Pain management: Consider stronger analgesia today (discussion of alternatives to ibuprofen); options discussed include Naproxen (NSAID), with paracetamol or codeine as adjuncts.
  - Medication optimization: Counseling on NSAID dosing; maximum dosing considerations discussed (the clinician noted dosing guidance and opportunity to adjust NSAID use).
  - Add-on therapy: Consider a short course of paracetamol and/or codeine as needed; Naproxen prescribed if appropriate.
  - Headache diary: Start a diary to identify triggers (diet, sleep, caffeine, stress, hydration) and response to treatment.
  - Follow-up: Return in 1–2 weeks; re-evaluate for migraine diagnosis and consider prophylaxis if headaches become more frequent.
  - Red flags: Advise to seek urgent care if vision loss, new focal deficits, fever, confusion, neck stiffness worsening, or severe worsening of symptoms.
  - Eye considerations: Given photophobia and visual discomfort, advise consideration of a repeat eye exam if symptoms persist or worsen; ensure glasses use and screen hygiene are optimized.

Issue 2: Considerations for tension-type headache or other primary headache
- Assessment: Presentation could be compatible with tension-type headache given diffuse, stress-associated features and high screen time; however, photophobia and nausea tilt toward migraine.
- Plan:
  - Non-pharmacologic strategies: Continue/adjust headache hygiene (hydration, regular meals, sleep routine, screen breaks, stress management).
  - Reassess in follow-up; if features evolve toward more typical tension-type pattern without photophobia/nausea, adjust plan accordingly.

Issue 3: Less likely but important to consider meningitis/encephalitis
- Assessment: Neck stiffness and photophobia raise concern for meningeal irritation; fever and altered mental status are not present.
- Plan:
  - Not currently suspected but keep in differential; instruct patient to seek urgent care if fever, confusion, neck stiffness worsens, or new neurologic deficits appear.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Migraine (without aura) with possible genetic predisposition
  - Likelihood: High
  - Rationale: Right-eye predominant, photophobia, nausea, progressive daily headache over 3 days, family history of migraines; past NSAID response supports primary headache pattern.
- Tension-type headache
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Rationale: Diffuse dull pain with work-related stress and high screen time; photophobia and nausea less typical for tension-type but overlapping features exist.
- Meningitis/encephalitis
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Rationale: Neck stiffness and photophobia present, but absence of fever, AMS, or focal deficits lowers probability; keep in mind in case of evolving symptoms.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements clinically expected for a consult:
  - Vitals (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature) not documented.
  - Formal medications reconciliation and allergy list not structured in note (allergies documented as "not known" in history; no formal allergy section completed).
  - Physical examination findings and neurological/eye exam results not documented.
  - Labs or imaging results none reported.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - No explicit conflicts detected; migraine is most consistent with history; meningitis considered but unlikely given lack of fever/altered mental status.
  - MOH noted in DDx as a possibility but not explicitly diagnosed in transcript; plan includes optimizing NSAID use and diary to assess.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall coherent; minor gaps and incomplete responses at times; some phrasing and punctuation issues in the initial portion but content sufficient to establish history and plan.

Document Quality (summary of elements to address in the chart):
- Allergies: confirm formal allergy status; currently documented as “not known.”
- Medications reconciliation: formal list not provided beyond ibuprofen use; ensure complete medication list at next visit.
- Vitals: obtain and document at next visit or during any urgent evaluation.
- Exam data: obtain and record comprehensive physical/neuro/ocular examination findings (pupil exam, funduscopic exam if indicated, neck stiffness assessment).
- Pending tests: none ordered at this visit; consider imaging only if red flags develop.

End of note.
